ideas.a: It is where two neurons meet (or a neuron meets a muscle)
A chemical is released from vesicles and crosses it
The impulse can only cross it one way

model: The place where two neurons meet; a chemical is released from vesicles and crosses over, so the impulse only passes one way.

ideas.a: It is released from vesicles at the end of an axon
It crosses to the next nerve cell and binds to its receptors
An enzyme breaks it down afterwards, or it is taken back in

model: A substance released from vesicles at a nerve ending; it diffuses across the tiny space to the next nerve cell and binds to its receptors, then enzymes break it down.

ideas.a: It is a coat wrapped round the axon
It makes the impulse travel faster
It is what makes white matter white

model: The pale lipid coat wrapped around an axon; it stops the impulse leaking away, so it travels much faster, and it is why white matter looks white.

ideas.a: It sits along the axon of a neuron
It makes the insulating fatty layer
Many of them lie along each axon, end to end

model: One of many found along a nerve fibre, it rolls itself round and round the axon, making the insulating fatty layer that speeds up impulses.

ideas.a: It is a short extension on the cell body
It picks up impulses from other neurons or receptors
It carries impulses towards the cell body

model: Short, many-fingered threads on a nerve's cell body that pick up impulses from other neurons and carry them towards the cell body.

ideas.a: It carries impulses away from the cell body
It is covered by the myelin sheath
It ends in knobs that release neurotransmitter

model: The single extended part of a neuron that carries impulses away from the cell body; it is wrapped in myelin and ends in knobs that release neurotransmitter.

ideas.a: It carries impulses into the spinal cord or brain
It starts where a stimulus is detected, e.g. in the skin
Its cell body is on a short side branch

model: Carries impulses from the skin and other detectors into the spinal cord or brain; its cell body sits on a short side branch.

ideas.a: It carries impulses out from the brain or spinal cord
It ends on a gland, or on something that contracts
Its cell body is at one end, with the dendrites

model: Carries impulses out from the spinal cord or brain to a gland or something that contracts; its cell body, with dendrites, is at one end.

ideas.a: It is found only inside the CNS (in the grey matter)
It passes impulses from sensory neurons to motor neurons
It is the middle neuron of a reflex arc

model: A short neuron found only inside the grey matter of the brain and spinal cord; it passes impulses from sensory neurons on to motor neurons.

ideas.a: It happens without thinking about it
It is a response to a stimulus
It is very fast and protects the body
For example blinking, or pulling a hand off something hot

model: A quick response to a stimulus that happens without you thinking, like blinking or pulling your hand off a hot pan; it protects you.

ideas.a: It is the organ in the skull and the tissue down the backbone
It is the body's control centre
It is wrapped in the meninges

model: The body's control headquarters: the organ inside the skull and the column of tissue running down inside the backbone, both wrapped in meninges.

ideas.a: There are three of them
They cover the brain and spinal cord
Cerebrospinal fluid fills the space between them

model: Three thin sheets of tissue wrapped around the brain and spinal cord, with cerebrospinal fluid between them; they shield the CNS from injury.

ideas.a: It is mostly the parts of neurons holding the nucleus, with little myelin
It is the core of the spinal cord, and the outer layer of the brain
It holds the interneurons and synapses

model: The darker tissue made of the parts of neurons that hold the nucleus, with little myelin; it forms the core of the spinal cord and the outer layer of the brain.

ideas.a: It is under the cerebrum, at the rear of the brain
It keeps posture steady and muscle movements smooth

model: The 'little brain' tucked under the cerebrum at the rear of the head; it keeps your posture steady and makes muscle movements smooth, like walking.

ideas.a: It fills the hollow centre of the spinal cord and spaces in the brain
It absorbs shocks and protects the CNS
It lies between the meninges

model: The clear watery stuff that fills the hollow centre of the spinal cord and the spaces round the brain, between the meninges; it absorbs shocks.

ideas.a: It is a neurotransmitter released at synapses in the brain
Too little of it causes shaking and stiffness
It makes you feel good and motivated, and drugs raise it

model: A brain chemical released at synapses that makes you feel good and motivated; drugs and junk food raise it, and too little causes shaking and stiffness.

ideas.a: They are the body's own painkillers
They are released during hard physical activity or laughter
They give a feeling of well-being, a 'high'

model: Brain chemicals released during a hard run or a big laugh; they dull hurt and give a feeling of well-being, the 'high' after a workout.
